title: Prove general-initial FTL and its actual recursive mean/count state
head: codex/research-online-ftl-state
body:
FTL's source description permits any first prediction in[0,1] (Orabona v10 printed3/PDF15), and its running-average discussion avoids storing the entire history (printed6/PDF18). Add a genuine recursive mean/count state and prove at every time that it equals the general-initial strict-past mean predictor. Extend existing Mean by the zero-inclusive successor identity; preserve all four earlier Mean proofs and every earlier FTL definition/proof. Nine new public proofs and three definitions close these two source subobligations, rather than nine additional book results.

Fix initial c before the data. State0=(0,c), then update (n,m) to(n+1,m+(yt-m)/(n+1)); the first update cancels c. All-real algebraic identities, with interval feasibility requiring only c and each strict-past label in[0,1]. Whole-state causality compares the same c. The half specialization identifies the same trajectory used by the existing quarter/refined/logarithmic bounds; no quarter or new rate is claimed for general c. This is a mathematical noncomputable exact-real pair, not fixed-bit memory/executable/runtime certification. Existing empirical-mean decomposition/minimization/feasibility/uniqueness producers establish the actual prefix leaders; no desired state/argmin/regret certificate premise.

Six validation proofs cover different initial states and their identical first update; varying means1/2 and2/3; changed current target only affecting the next state; feasible initial1 versus ambient outside-initial2; half-state two-round regret3/4 via the prior theorem; and feasible initial1,target0 giving first loss1>1/4. These are validation results, not additional book theorems.
